papers.title: Spin Conductivity: Insight From Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: The investigation on the spin conductivity has now been blooming in burgeoning altermagnetic materials. Here, an alternative and elementary derivation for the spin conductivity expression is presented. This is done within the context of perturbation theory. It indicates that our derived expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-even ($\mathcal{T}$ for time reversal) spin conductivity agrees exactly with those derived from the Kubo linear response theory and quantum kinetic theory. In addition, the expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-odd spin conductivity in the clean limit is exactly consistent with those presented previously. We show that the $\mathcal{T}$-odd ($\mathcal{T}$-even) spin conductivity arises from the contribution of zeroth-order (first-order) wave function correction. Our work provides some physical insight into the spin conductivity from the perturbation theory and shines more light on the charge-to-spin conversion mechanism in magnetic materials.

papers.title: Crystal and magnetic structures of MnSi in zero magnetic field: Neutron diffraction and symmetry analysis
papers.abstract: Combining high-resolution wide-angle neutron powder diffraction with magnetic-superspace symmetry analysis, we refine the crystal structure and present, to our knowledge, the first systematic refinement of cubic $P2_13$ MnSi's zero-field magnetic structure across multiple magnetic satellite families. We compare single-arm rhombohedral 3+1D and cubic four-arm 3+4D magnetic superspace-group (MSSG) descriptions with propagation vectors along $\langle111\rangle$. Simultaneous extinction of the two satellite groups around $\{100\}$ dictates a transverse circular-helix model. This suppression and refinements of 18 separately varied satellite-group intensities support this ideal limit with only one adjustable magnetic amplitude. In the ideal single-arm model with MSSG $R3.1'(0,0,g)ts$, the moment has constant magnitude 0.535(3) $\mu_B$ per Mn. An explicit four-arm 3+4D cubic superspace construction presented here combines four interpenetrating helices and, for the illustrated phase choice, has moments ranging from zero to 0.874(5) $\mu_B$ per Mn, with the same root-mean-square moment as the 3+1D structure. Their identical powder profiles prevent the present measurements from distinguishing them. The average crystal structure remains cubic within experimental resolution, providing structural motivation for the cubic magnetic model. The mean lattice parameter, determined with formal relative precision $\sigma_a/a \lesssim 10^{-5}$, exhibits nonmonotonic temperature dependence below the N\'eel temperature.

papers.title: Schottky barrier height modulation and memristive behavior in a mechanically exfoliated $MoS_2$ flake with multiple lateral electrodes
papers.abstract: Van de Waals materials possess great potential as core active materials for novel electronics, optoelectronics, and sensing applications. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and other low-dimensional materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and binary oxides exhibit memristive behavior, making them attractive candidates as building blocks for resistive memories and neuromorphic computing devices. In this work, we investigate two-terminal lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few layer $MoS_2$ flakes. We study the influence of the Schottky barrier height (SBH) as a function of the contact area. We report different SBHs from 60 meV up to 208 meV in the same $MoS_2$ flake and analyze the effect of the SBH in the memristive-like $J-V_{DS}$ curves and the observed non-volatile/volatile resistance switching. Our results highlight the importance of contact engineering to obtain different memristive properties in $MoS_2$-based devices.

papers.title: Compensation Domain Walls in Ferrimagnets as Spin-Torque Oscillator Candidates
papers.abstract: Spin-torque nano-oscillators are promising nanoscale microwave sources, yet their performance is often limited by narrow operational ranges and sensitivity to device parameters. Here, we numerically investigate the dynamics of compensation domain walls in ferrimagnetic systems driven by spin-transfer torque as a microwave source candidate. These walls arise in structures with adjacent regions of different compensation character, where the competition between exchange and Zeeman energies under an applied magnetic field stabilizes a distinct magnetic texture. We demonstrate steady current-driven rotation of compensation domain walls over a broad range of current densities within the model. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we develop a collective-coordinate model and derive an analytical expression for the oscillation frequency, which quantitatively reproduces the dependence on current and magnetic field observed in micromagnetic simulations. Our results identify compensation domain walls as a candidate platform for tunable spin-torque nano-oscillators with intrinsic field-induced confinement.

papers.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
papers.abstract: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

papers.title: Magnetic behavior of the $5d^1$ Re-based double perovskite Sr$_2$ZnReO$_6$
papers.abstract: The subtle interplay between spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, and cation ordering can lead to exotic magnetic states in transition-metal ions. We report a comprehensive study of the Re-based (5$d^1$) ordered double perovskite oxide Sr$_2$ZnReO$_6$ combining synchrotron x-ray diffraction (XRD), magnetic susceptibility, muon spin relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. XRD reveals that Sr$_2$ZnReO$_6$ crystallizes in the monoclinic structure (space group $P2_1/n$) at low temperature. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate a transition below $\sim$13 K, with $M$--$H$ loops showing ferromagnetic-like hysteresis and an unusually high coercive field of 23 kOe at 2 K. Zero-field $\mu$SR measurements detect static and spatially disordered internal fields below $T_M \simeq $ 12 K, consistent with a canted antiferromagnetic ground state determined by detailed DFT and force-theorem in Hubbard-I calculations. The reduced high-temperature effective moment ($\sim0.76~\mu_B$) and very small static moment ($\lesssim 0.2~\mu_B$) derived from $\mu$SR analysis and local-field simulations indicate a decisive role of spin-orbit coupling. Through a combined experimental and computational approach we unambiguously determine the canted antiferromagnetic order in Sr$_2$ZnReO$_6$, showing that a very small ordered moment coexists with an exceptionally large coercivity. These results underscore the crucial role of spin-orbit coupling and orbital ordering, providing new insights into magnetism in 5$d^1$ double perovskites.

papers.title: Quartet ferromagnetism in the small-exchange limit
papers.abstract: Rare-earth magnets are often regarded as classical owing to their large angular momentum J, but this picture breaks down when exchange is smaller than the crystalline electric-field (CEF) energy scale, allowing the degeneracy of low-lying CEF manifolds to dictate the emergent quantum phases. Here, we uncover such a regime in the RV6Sn6 (R = rare-earth) kagome metals with strong magnetic anisotropy. Thermodynamic and neutron-diffraction measurements reveal successive axial and tilted ferromagnetic (FM) phases in DyV6Sn6, arising from independent ordering of the axial Mz and transverse Mx dipolar components enabled by a rare quasi-quartet ground state. On the other hand, HoV6Sn6 has a similar tilted magnetic anisotropy, but remains axial down to 0.03 K. This discrepancy can be traced back to the non-Kramers nature of Ho3+ where the CEF lifts the quartet degeneracy, leaving a quasi-triplet ground state. Unlike quartets or higher multiplets, we find that the effective spin-1 triplet does not allow independent dipolar ordering without strong quadrupolar (nematic) interactions that act to break rotational symmetry, revealing an essential multipolar prerequisite for tilted magnetic ground states. These results establish a quartet CEF manifold as the minimal degeneracy required for dipolar-driven independent ordering. Mapping the surrounding CEF parameter space further reveals competing magnetic, non-magnetic singlet, and potential quadrupolar phases, driven by multifold ground state degeneracies. These results establish CEF tuning as a versatile route to unconventional quantum phases across the broader RT6X6 (T = transition metal; X = Sn, Ge) family.

papers.title: Pauli propagation in adaptive local frames
papers.abstract: The cost of Pauli propagation depends on the local basis in which the evolving operator is expanded. We show that its Pauli complexity splits into an occupation part, invariant under local rotations and bounded from below by the operator mass and length distributions, and a flavour part that a suitable basis can remove. We introduce frame-adaptive Pauli propagation (FAPP), which rotates the basis of every qubit, gate by gate, to the principal axes of the operator's local polarisation, exactly and within the memory structure of Pauli propagation. This simple rule achieves most of what the best local frame can, and the polarisation predicts how much any local frame can gain. In the Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields, FAPP lowers the truncation error at fixed memory by up to an order of magnitude and the memory by a size-independent factor of three; on the infinite two-dimensional lattice it needs up to seven times fewer strings for a given certified accuracy, and in Clifford circuits doped with T gates two to eight times fewer.

papers.title: Extending the reach of real-space real-time TDDFT: new developments in the Octopus code
papers.abstract: Octopus is an open-source package implementing time-dependent density functional theory in a real-space, real-time formulation. Here we report on the developments since our previous contribution to the Special Topic Issue on Electronic Structure Software [J. Chem. Phys. 152, 124119 (2020)]. New exchange-correlation functionals extend the range of systems that can be treated, while advances in relativistic and all-electron methods open the door to core-electron spectroscopy. New capabilities for lattice dynamics - stress-tensor calculation, geometry optimization, support for machine-learned force fields, and phonon calculations - enable a fully ab initio description of light-induced lattice dynamics in real time. We also present developments that move beyond the dipole approximation, capturing light-matter interaction more faithfully. Improved methods for exciton dynamics complement a set of algorithmic advances - new propagation schemes, imaginary-time evolution, and a refactored grid handling more than a billion points - that together substantially improve performance and scalability. Combined with technical improvements such as AMD GPU support and a modernized build system, these developments consolidate Octopus as a versatile, high-performance platform for exploring electronic excitations, light-matter interaction, and nonequilibrium dynamics in molecules, nanostructures, and extended systems.

papers.title: Kerr-athermal baths enhance cooling in quantum refrigerators
papers.abstract: We study a three-qubit quantum refrigerator, with a three-body interaction enabling cooling of the target qubit, coupled to harmonic oscillator baths prepared in stationary Kerr-athermal states. The reservoir occupation probabilities are specified by a Kerr-type preparation Hamiltonian, while the bath dynamics during operation are harmonic. We show that these reservoirs lower the steady-state temperature of the cold qubit relative to the thermal-bath reference. The improvement of steady-state cooling is distinct from that of the minimum transient temperature, which is not universally enhanced. In a parameter regime where the thermal reference exhibits only transient cold-qubit cooling, the engineered Kerr-athermal baths can produce a steady-state temperature below the initial value. We also investigate the dependence of the steady-state temperature and minimum attainable temperatures on the anharmonicity in the bath state. Analysis of bath-currents reveals lower steady-state temperatures with nearly unchanged coefficients of performance, revealing that reservoir engineering leads to cold-qubit cooling.

papers.title: Critical Phases of the extended isotropic $XY$ chain with four-spin interaction
papers.abstract: Using the Jordan-Wigner transformation we calculate exactly the ground state and low-temperature thermodynamic properties of the spin $S=1/2$ isotropic $XX$ chain with four spin interaction. In terms of the equivalent spinless fermion (SF) representation the system is viewed as a lattice fermion gas with nearest-neighbor ($J$) and next-next-next-neighbor ($J^{\ast}/4$) hopping. It is shown that with the increase of four spin coupling, at $J^{\ast}_{c} = 4J/3$ the system experiences the Lifshitz type topological phase transition characterized by the tripling of Fermi points. The quantum phase transition (QPT) point marks transition from a gapless spin-liquid phase of standard $XX$ chain into again a gapless spin-liquid phase with different character of power-low decay of spin correlations. At the transition point the free fermion dispersion relation shows flattering at Fermi points, what determines singular character of density of states $\rho(\omega)\sim (\omega/J)^{-2/3}$ and as a consequence unconventional temperature dependence of heat capacity of the system $C\sim (T/J^{\ast})^{1/3}$, and singular magnetic susceptibility of the system $\chi(H)\sim (H/J^{\ast})^{-2/3}$. In the case of alternating magnetic field the system is characterized by the rich ground state phase diagram which contains fully polarized (ferromagnetic), gapped antiferromagnetic (AFM) and spin liquid phases. At the transition point from the gapped AFM phase into the gapless polarized spin liquid phase the system shows rapid increase of magnetization $m\sim(H-H_c)^{1/6}$ and magnetic susceptibility a singular behavior as $\chi(H)\sim (H-H_c)^{-5/6}$.

papers.title: Reentrant Localization Length in a Quasiperiodic Thue-Morse Chain
papers.abstract: We investigate single-particle localization in a dimerized Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain whose quasiperiodic onsite potential is masked by the deterministic Thue--Morse sequence. The behavior is characterized by the transfer-matrix Lyapunov exponent, and by the participation moments of exactly diagonalized chains. For intracell-dominated hopping the mid-spectrum Lyapunov exponent depends nonmonotonically on the potential strength, developing a pronounced minimum that enhances the localization length by an order of magnitude over an intermediate window, whereas an intercell-dominated chain responds monotonically. The exponent remains positive at every sampled nonzero potential strength and at every state of the spectral sector, and the second participation moment saturates over the full range of system sizes, so the intermediate window is an enhancement of a finite localization length and not a change of localization class. Finite-size generalized dimensions follow the same response in real space and in the Fourier-conjugate representation, while their moment-order separation decreases systematically with size. Controlled sign masks identify the origin: the response requires short-range sign anticorrelation aligned with the dominant bonds, and displacing the modulation by a single site, which destroys the exactness of that anticorrelation while leaving the sequence otherwise intact, removes the response entirely. An effective-dimer description relates the alignment to the division of the onsite modulation between the internal detuning of a bonded pair and its common-mode energy.

papers.title: Quasi-periodicity enforces Berry phase discontinuity in crystals
papers.abstract: The Berry phase of an isolated electronic state is evaluated for different integration paths in reciprocal space, thanks to Riemann-Bloch states providing a consistent description in the whole Brillouin zone. The relationship with the bounded position operator is investigated for the open-path Berry phase and with different form factors of the constituent Gaussian type atomic orbitals (GTOs). When the Berry phase is evaluated over a closed loop in reciprocal space, a regularisation procedure in the complex plane is adopted and additional \textit{quasi}-symmetries are exploited here for the first time in order to rationalise the occurrence of non-analytical jumps as a function of the winding number or of the GTO broadening.

papers.title: Piecewise Parabolic Kinetic Energies and Classical Time Crystals
papers.abstract: We present explicit, exact analytic solutions for classical time crystals embedded in a parabolic potential for the position. While Lagrangians with a quartic kinetic energy yield complex trajectories governed by inscrutable elliptic integrals, we demonstrate that unconventional piecewise parabolic kinetic energies -minimized at nonzero values of the speed- admit simple, transparent periodic solutions. In these systems, the speed acquires definite periodic discontinuities but remains always nonzero. The requirement that the action be the smallest available determines the branch that the solution will follow, ensuring in addition that it is stable there and rendering the Hamiltonian single-valued as a function of momentum. Furthermore, we introduce a powerful piecewise parabolic emulation framework to approximate highly non-linear kinetic energies, demonstrating its utility on both quartic time crystals and the relativistic harmonic oscillator. We show that finding exact solutions to these emulated models provides accurate, physically transparent simulacra of complicated problems, offering a robust alternative to standard numerical approximations for non-quadratic kinetic energies.
